name: Langtang rock-ice avalanche
headline: ~2 km² of rock and ice fell 1,400 m from 5,150 m (energy like M5.5).

sections.The setup: Very warm Jul–Aug; more rain than snow; freezing level up ~100 m/decade; glacier retreat 1–2.3%/yr.
sections.The trigger: ~2 km² of rock and ice fell 1,400 m from 5,150 m (energy like M5.5).
sections.What amplified it: Became a debris flood at ~188 km/h; 5,850 m³/s at Devghat; 30.5 million m³ of debris.
sections.Climate signal: Warming raised local Jul–Aug heat ~1.5 °C; geology the root cause (WWA).
sections.Still open: Summary entry: the full deep-dive (day-by-day timeline, steering, how it ended, sources) has not been written yet. It will be added as the log works back through the year.
